text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 99th-percentile latency observed for embeddings-serving in eu-west1 since ~08:02 UTC. Error rate is low, but token-level latency up ~3-4x for some routes. Auto-mitigation didn’t trigger. Paging kevin-sre and oncall team.
kevin-sre: saw it. I’m on it. adding logging to compare KV cache hit rates first. can someone confirm if any deploys happened ~07:50-08:00?
maria-eng: no deploys in eu-west1 from infra. we rolled a model catalog refresh in control plane at 07:45 but that shouldn't touch serving nodes.
ashok-platform: checking autoscaler logs, nothing unusual. cluster shows a subset of GPUs hitting high PCIe wait times. suspect driver-level jitter on a handful of nodes.
kevin-sre: ok — plan: 1) divert new embedding requests for experiments tier to eu-central fallback pool, 2) drain the 3 affected serving hosts in eu-west1 for a rolling restart, 3) temporarily route critical customers to quantized fallback model (gptq-embed-lite) if latency still high. doing step 1 now.
sam-devex: statuspage draft for public shows degraded performance for embeddings in eu-west1 only. Drafting customer note as well. dropping both in thread for quick reviews.
ops-lead: good. please include guidance for customers with latency-sensitive pipelines (recommend switching to eu-central or using async batch endpoints).
julia-support: I'll prep targeted outreach for customers with active support tickets in the last 24h and flag any enterprise SLAs.
kevin-sre: routing update applied to service-router: diverting ~20% of traffic to eu-central fallback for experiments tier. watch requests now.
oncall-bot: Pager routed to kevin-sre at 2432109900. Reminder: follow incident runbook for embedding latency (runbook id: runbook/embeddings-latency-v3).
kevin-sre: digging into Prometheus panels. KV cache hit ratio dropped from 0.89 to 0.46 on the three nodes. Could be cold cache due to restarts or network blip.
maria-eng: I can trigger KV cache preload after restart; add warmup job to the drain sequence.
kevin-sre: initiating node drain for shard hosts: host-euw-12, host-euw-15, host-euw-19. Command:
```
# drain host (example)
infractl node drain --region eu-west1 --host host-euw-12 --reason "latency spike investigation"
```
kevin-sre: starting host-euw-12 drain at 08:14 UTC.
ashok-platform: driver logs show repeated NVLINK resets on host-euw-15. scheduling reboot for that host.
maria-eng: adding cache-warmup hook in drain pipeline:
```
post-drain-hook: runwarmup --model gptq-embed-lite --keys /warmup/emb-keys-1
```
sam-devex: statuspage/public draft (please review):
```
Components: Embeddings API (eu-west1) — degraded performance
Impact: Increased latency, intermittent slow responses for embedding and similarity routes in eu-west1. Not all users affected. No data loss.
Current status: Investigating — team is draining affected hosts and routing traffic to alternate region.
Estimated next update: in 30 minutes.
```
ops-lead: +1. add advice: "If you rely on low-latency embeddings, consider switching to eu-central region temporarily. We apologize for the disruption."
julia-support: customer email/snippet draft:
```
Subject: Temporary performance degradation for embeddings in eu-west1
Hi <customer>,
We’re investigating increased latency for embeddings in eu-west1. Our engineers are draining a small set of serving hosts and routing some traffic to other regions. If you have latency-sensitive pipelines, please consider routing to eu-central or using async batch requests as a temporary workaround. We’ll update you within 30 minutes or sooner.
Apologies for the inconvenience — support@example.com
```
kevin-sre: host-euw-12 drain completed at 08:25 UTC, restarted GPU driver, cache warmup succeeded (hit ratio back to 0.78). Observed 20% latency improvement for that shard.
maria-eng: good. proceeding with host-euw-15 reboot now.
ashok-platform: host-euw-15 reboot scheduled and completed at 08:37 UTC. NVLINK errors cleared. cache warmup underway.
kevin-sre: after host-euw-15 back online, overall 99p latency is down ~1.8x from peak but still 1.6x above baseline. moving host-euw-19 drain next.
maria-eng: host-euw-19 drain started 08:45 UTC. small config tweak: disable preemptible-bursting on that host during warmup.
oncall-bot: handoff reminder: kevin-sre to hand to next oncall at 09:00 UTC if stable for 15m.
sam-devex: updating statuspage with mitigation note and ETA now:
```
Update: Mitigation in progress — affected nodes are being restarted and traffic is being routed to a fallback region. Partial improvements observed. Next update in 20 minutes.
```
kevin-sre: host-euw-19 restarted and warmup finished at 08:58 UTC. KV hit ratio aggregated is now 0.86.
kevin-sre: metrics show 95p and 99p latencies now within 1.1x baseline. rolling routing back traffic to eu-west1. will monitor for 15m.
maria-eng: removing temporary model downgrade flag for critical customers. all warmup hooks validated.
julia-support: sending short customer update to all impacted customers and enterprise contacts. template used.
ops-lead: great. prepare for handoff: kevin-sre -> oncall-next (kevin will mark stable then handoff). Please include postmortem owner assignment.
kevin-sre: marking statuspage RESOLVED at 09:12 UTC with note and: assigning postmortem owner: kevin-sre. short blurb for statuspage completion and full postmortem ETA (24-48h):
```
Resolved: Root cause appears to be transient NVLINK resets on a small subset of hosts that caused cache thrashing and elevated PCIe wait. Affected hosts were restarted and cache warmup applied. Full postmortem and long-term mitigation plan will be posted within 48 hours.
```
oncall-bot: incident closed by kevin-sre at 2432113700.
julia-support: customer completion note sent at 09:15 UTC. included recommended next steps and offer for 1:1 help migrating to eu-central.
sam-devex: internal comms snippet for eng-all:
"Embeddings latency spike in eu-west1 this morning impacted 99p latency for some routes. NVLINK resets on three hosts triggered cache thrash. Hosts were rebooted and cache warmups applied; service restored. Postmortem coming."
ops-lead: nice concise. make sure runbook is updated with NVLINK detection and automated reboot flag. assign to ashok-platform.
ashok-platform: will add NVLINK detector and auto-reboot rule to the autoscaler playbook. filing PR shortly.
kevin-sre: thanks everyone. tagging for followups: @ashok-platform (autoscaler rule), @maria-eng (warmup hooks), @julia-support (customer comms), @sam-devex (statuspage/postmortem).
